title: every-datarecorder-declares-when-it-was-started-last-read-and-how-often-it-expects-reading
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> [TICKETME:waiting] -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(declared-cadence-discriminates) -> PROVED
intention: Every datarecorder carries when it started, when it was last read, how often it expects to be read, and whether it drains or reports-and-holds — so an unread recorder raises a trouble by itself instead of waiting to be noticed.
why: A datarecorder nobody reads accumulates silently — the same shape as the inspector findings that 'accumulated silently' until today. Akien 2026-09-04: with started/lastread/expected_read_frequency on every recorder, 'we can also automatically issue trouble tickets on unread data recorders.' The lived symptom is data written for a reader who never comes, discovered by accident.
how: SETTLED AT THE CAST 2026-09-07 (the 'names are Akien's' reason is retired by his ruling that nothing before PROVEME waits at his gate). A `reading.json` berths beside `records.jsonl` inside the recorder's own directory at ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/tools/data_recorder/<name>/ — the holder's instance home, which is where Law 6 already puts a tool's ongoing state, so the holder owns and gates it and the tool gates nothing of its own. Four fields: `started` (ISO, written by the recorder on its FIRST write() — not on construction, because BaseDevice mints a recorder for every device on every boot and a construction stamp would silently mean 'last booted'), `last_read` (ISO or null), `expected_read_frequency_seconds` (int or null), `on_read` ('drain' | 'hold'). A reader stamps through one new door, DataRecorder.stamp_read(ids=None), which moves last_read and — when on_read is 'drain' and ids were given — calls the existing clear(ids) in the same act, so a reader cannot stamp without draining or drain without stamping. Declaration comes from the DEVICE: DataRecorder.__init__ takes the two optional settings and BaseDevice passes through what the device declares. UNDECLARED IS RED, NOT DEFAULT (Law 9) — there is no fallback frequency, because a fallback would silently green the recorders that have no reader at all, and that is the hollow build (Law 8). A new at-rest probe on the existing probe surface (NOT new ground-loop work) globs the recorders through cairn.tools.base.address, never a hand-spelled path, and raises via DiagnosticBase.raise_trouble — no import of the trouble device and no bus (ticket 9579a6f9cec6). TWO DISTINCT IDENTITIES, deliberately not folded: 'recorder-declares-no-reader-<device>-<instance>-<name>' and 'recorder-read-overdue-<device>-<instance>-<name>'. Merging them would tell the reader that 'nobody ever specified this' and 'somebody specified it and missed' are the same defect, and they are opposite instructions.
falsifier: DONE when a recorder deliberately left unread past its declared frequency raises a trouble on the next beat, and a recorder read on time does not — both halves, because the half that only fires is a check that cannot fail. THIRD TOOTH added at the cast: a recorder declaring nothing raises its own distinct identity ('declares no reader'), separate from 'read is overdue'. WRONG INTENT if most recorders have no meaningful reader cadence — then the switch (drain vs hold) is the whole feature and the frequency is noise. NOTE, measured: with 10/10 recorders unread today the frequency's DISCRIMINATING power is untestable until readers exist, which is exactly what the WATCHME below watches for.
traces_to: Law 7 — an unread record is a silent error; Law 3 — 'expected read frequency' makes the claim that something is read measurable. Law 10 — the recorder can measure its own reading.

watchme.trigger: On each at-rest beat, after the overdue check runs: record the population — how many recorders declare a frequency, how many declare none, how many have a non-null last_read, and the spread of declared frequencies. It fires on the beat because the data is already in hand; it costs one extra dict.
watchme.enough: Enough when at least three recorders have a non-null last_read (real readers exist) AND the declared frequencies have taken at least two distinct values. Then the question is answered either way: if the overdue troubles discriminate — some recorders green, some red — the frequency is load-bearing and the watch closes green; if every reader reads on every beat or every declaration collapses to one value, the WRONG INTENT clause is confirmed, the drain/hold switch was the whole feature, and the watch closes by kicking a ticket to strip the frequency. Deliberately NOT time-bounded: with 10/10 recorders unread, a clock would only measure how long readers take to appear, which is a different question.
watchme.carrier: A verdict artifact against this ticket's WRONG INTENT clause, written by the probe on the beat it reaches `enough`, carrying the population counts and the distinct-frequency set as its evidence rather than a summary of them.
watchme.nexus: The data_recorder tool's own charter tree at cairn/tools/data_recorder/ — the verdict amends the charter's account of what a recorder is FOR (a mailbox with a reader, or a mailbox that holds), which is the claim the census already put in doubt.
watchme.consumer: CC, through the operator inbox — the same surface the overdue troubles land on, so the answer arrives where the question is already visible.

owner: cairn device owns folder-based datarecorders (press_office is one). The field names and the drain/hold switch were settled at the cast, 2026-09-07, under Akien's ruling that nothing before PROVEME waits at his gate.
author: CC
cast_under: Akien 2026-09-07 (idea 811780d76281): 'the goal before we let go of fable is to move everything that doesn't have the word cognition in it to BUILDME'
measured_at_cast: CENSUS 2026-09-07, and it is the finding this ticket now stands on: 10 records.jsonl on disk holding 1,817 records — harbor_master 1429, librarian 156, codemother 59, charter 46, press_office 40, cairn 32, tester 31, disk_only 12, test_no_verb_device 9, inference_domain 3. Exactly 2 construction sites (cairn/tools/base/device.py:240, cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/discovered.py:103) and ZERO readers: nothing in the corpus calls .read() or .clear() on a recorder outside that recorder's own proofs. Every one is BaseDevice.receive()'s default sink for verbless mail — mail arrives, is recorded 'for later evaluation', and nothing evaluates. This CONFIRMS the why rather than killing the ticket ('data written for a reader who never comes, discovered by accident'), and it prices the design: undeclared-is-red fires on all ten the first beat after this lands, which under the trouble damper is ten tickets at count 1 — the improvement backlog doing its job, not a flood.

gates_bound.proved_by: cairn/tools/data_recorder/proofs/test_reading_declaration.py, sealed through TesterDevice.run_proof. Teeth: (1) overdue raises on a frozen clock; (2) inside-frequency raises NOTHING; (3) undeclared raises a DIFFERENT identity; (4) stamp_read drains-and-stamps under 'drain', stamps only under 'hold'; (5) `started` is written on first write(), not on construction. Teeth 2 and 5 fail if the feature is stubbed green (Law 8).
gates_bound.feeds_back_to_origin_on_failure: A red at PROVEME kicks back to BUILDME through cairn.tools.base.transitions.emit; the probe's own troubles are the standing operational feedback and land in the operator inbox on the beat.
gates_bound.at_rest_probe_gate: the WATCHME emission gate resolves ARMED from the probe berth; the probe must exist on disk before PROVEME -> WATCHME crosses.
gates_bound.check_type: deterministic — a clock comparison and a file read, no LLM in the fire path.

children: none, because this is a leaf: one tool file, one pass-through in cairn/tools/base/device.py, one probe, one proof. The three teeth are teeth in one proof, not separable nodes — tooth 2 is only meaningful beside tooth 1. The reader that would eventually call stamp_read is NOT a child and must not become one: this ticket measures the absence of reading, and building its own consumer would green its own measurement.
